scope: Production English article/search runtime and Chromium accessibility tree

findings.summary: The light/dark toggle exposes neither its selected state nor a changing action name.
findings.fix: Use a native checkbox or button role=switch with aria-checked, or a toggle button with aria-pressed and stable Dark mode name; synchronize initial and changed state in blocking.js. Alternatively announce the next action with a changing button name.
findings.evidence: Chromium AX tree before/after click exposes the same button name Toggle between dark and light theme and no checked/pressed state; body.theme-dark changes false to true. aria-label overrides the CSS-switched inner Light mode/Dark mode text.

findings.summary: The visually highlighted current navigation page is not identified programmatically.
findings.fix: When matching the current pathname, set aria-current=page on that link alongside the active class. Ensure exactly the current page link is marked.
findings.evidence: On /en/how-to-guides/manage-pages/ the link has class navigation__link active; CSS changes its background and foreground. Its Chromium AX properties contain URL/focusable only, with no current state.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation toggle advertises an ARIA menu popup although its content is ordinary navigation.
findings.fix: Remove aria-haspopup=true from this disclosure button; retain the updated aria-expanded state and optionally add aria-controls pointing to an ID on the navigation container. Keep native navigation links instead of adding menu roles.
findings.evidence: The toggle has aria-haspopup=true (equivalent to menu), but opens <nav class=primary-nav><ul> with ordinary links rather than a menu widget. mobile-menu/index.js correctly updates aria-expanded.

passed: Shared controls use native buttons, links and text inputs rather than custom div roles.
Mobile navigation expanded state is updated on open and close in source and captured runtime.
Copy and language dropdown triggers initialize aria-expanded=false; Bootstrap dropdown owns state transitions.
Shared decorative icons use aria-hidden=true with parent text or accessible names.
No authored broken aria-labelledby/aria-describedby/aria-controls references were found in scoped templates.
notes: Search modal dialog name/focus behavior and live-region behavior are owned by separate domain specialists and are not duplicated here.

Duplicate search IDs do not produce an absent Chromium accessible name: placeholder fallback names the modal field. The finding concerns the demonstrably broken explicit label relationship under 1.3.1, not removed WCAG 4.1.1.

Language names in the selector use hreflang but no lang; adding lang to each localized label improves pronunciation. Single-word language names are not asserted as a clear 3.1.2 failure because that criterion has exceptions for proper names and indeterminate words.
On-page contents are ordinary native fragment links; no custom tree, tab or menu semantics are needed.
No screenshots captured or inspected; runtime evidence consists of DOM and Chromium accessibility-tree data.
Broken modal search label relationship is confirmed in raw/aria-runtime.json and reported by forms-specialist, avoiding duplicate issue counts.
